differential_evidence.description: Birth history and early neonatal course: presence of a collodion membrane or neonatal scaling/ectropion strongly favors autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (lamellar) over ichthyosis vulgaris or X‑linked; absence of collodion and onset around several months favors ichthyosis vulgaris.

Scale morphology and distribution on skin exam: fine, white superficial scaling with extensor predominance, flexural sparing, keratosis pilaris, and palmoplantar hyperlinearity supports ichthyosis vulgaris; large brown plate‑like adherent scales favor X‑linked ichthyosis; thick, plate‑like generalized scaling with ectropion favors lamellar ichthyosis.

Family history pattern and associated findings: affected males in maternal lineage, and possible cryptorchidism or corneal changes, point to X‑linked ichthyosis; autosomal dominant vertical transmission or personal/family history of atopy favors ichthyosis vulgaris; consanguinity or unaffected parents with affected child point toward autosomal recessive ARCI.

Targeted laboratory/genetic/biochemical tests: FLG mutation testing (positive → confirms ichthyosis vulgaris); STS gene deletion or low steroid sulfatase activity (positive → confirms X‑linked ichthyosis); ARCI gene panel (TGM1, etc.) identifying biallelic pathogenic variants (positive → confirms lamellar/ARCI).
